definitions.explanation: the controlled cultivation of aquatic organisms like fish, shellfish, and seaweed
artificially cultivating organisms under controlled conditions

examples.japanese: {養殖|ようしょく}のサーモンを{買|か}った。
この{地域|ちいき}では{牡蠣|かき}の{養殖|ようしょく}が{盛|さか}んだ。
examples.english: Oyster farming is thriving in this area.

examples.japanese: {天然|てんねん}と{養殖|ようしょく}では{味|あじ}が{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: Wild-caught and farmed fish taste different.

examples.japanese: {真珠|しんじゅ}の{養殖|ようしょく}は{日本|にほん}で{始|はじ}まった。
{養殖|ようしょく}{真珠|しんじゅ}の{品質|ひんしつ}は{年々|ねんねん}{向上|こうじょう}している。
examples.english: The quality of cultured pearls is improving year by year.

examples.japanese: {海苔|のり}の{養殖|ようしょく}は{冬|ふゆ}に{行|おこな}われる。
examples.english: Seaweed farming is done in winter.

notes:
JAPANESE AQUACULTURE:
Japan is a major aquaculture producer, especially for:
- {鮭|さけ}/サーモン - salmon
- {鯛|たい} - sea bream
- {牡蠣|かき} - oysters
- {海苔|のり} - seaweed/nori
- うなぎ - eel
- {鮪|まぐろ} - tuna (recent developments)
- ホタテ - scallops

PEARL CULTIVATION:
{養殖|ようしょく}{真珠|しんじゅ} (cultured pearls) were pioneered by {御木本|みきもと}{幸吉|こうきち} (Mikimoto Kokichi) in Japan.

OPPOSITE:
- {天然|てんねん} - wild-caught, natural
- {天然|てんねん}{物|もの} - wild-caught (product)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {養殖|ようしょく}{業|ぎょう} - aquaculture industry
- {養殖|ようしょく}{場|じょう} - fish farm
- {養殖|ようしょく}{魚|ぎょ} - farmed fish
